title: Unpick a seam without damaging the fabric
instruction: Remove the six tacking stitches joining the canvas patches without cutting or tearing either patch. Put the seam ripper down when finished.
context: Repairing and reusing textiles requires removing embedded thread while preserving the surrounding fabric.
setup: Two flexible 75 × 80 × 0.4 mm cotton-canvas patches hang with a 20 mm overlap. Six red 0.8 mm polyester tacking loops pass through twelve 1.6 mm square needle holes per patch. A bench sewing clamp with a force-limited passive rear jaw holds the upper patch’s top 8 mm; the lower patch’s bottom edge rests on the real table to avoid dropping into the stitches. The current backing candidate adds a 65 mm wide rear board and front guide rails with a 26 mm seam-access window; neither patch is attached to the board. A 19 g seam ripper lies unheld beside the fixture. Dimensions and positions are in README.md.
scoring: Draft: 0.25 for two or three fully removed stitches, 0.5 for four or five, 0.75 for all six, and 1.0 for all six with no thread bridge and the seam ripper resting on the table at least 10 mm from either patch, released by the robot. Thread fragments must be visibly clear of both patches. Any new cut or tear extending over 2 mm beyond an original hole makes every score zero. Cutting a stitch alone does not count as removal. See JUDGING.md.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); proposed, not yet demonstrated.
reset_notes: Use a fresh pair of patches with six stitches in the same layout. Rebuild the native scene for each current development probe.
fidelity: Development candidate: each canvas patch comprises 118 free 0.4 mm rectangular rigid panels joined by 189 passive bending hinges. The sheet bends but is approximately inextensible; coarse panels and square needle holes simplify woven fabric. Each thread loop has 24 native capsule segments with contact, free twist and passive straight-rest bending. Thread bending stiffness is an engineering approximation informed by measured thinner polyester thread, not a calibration of this 0.8 mm strand. A 12 g spring jaw and backing support the cloth through ordinary contact without attachments. The intact native setup retained all stitches for two seconds. Sustained blade force is intended to sever thread joints; cut-end contact activation is under validation after an artificial-impulse failure. Complete cutting, extraction, visible fabric integrity and the robot demonstration remain unvalidated; no task score is claimed.
scores: Not run. CPU geometry and rule tests are not task scores.
